title: PM-Eng 1:1 prep — API / Console / Dedicated / Private
content:
Meeting: Diego (ENG lead) 1:1
Date: 2026-03-04 (prep) — meeting scheduled 2026-03-05 10:00am PT
Purpose: sync on priorities across API, Console rollout work, Dedicated pricing/quotas, and Private onboarding gaps. Align on decisions I need from Diego and what he needs from Product.

Agenda (30–40m):
1) Quick updates (5m) — personal, team capacity
2) Hosted API telemetry & quota changes (8m)
3) Console: rollout for per-route cost breakdown + rollout gating (8m)
4) Dedicated: pricing negotiation request from finance + perf headroom (6m)
5) Private deployment onboarding blockers (8m)
6) Action items & decisions (5m)

Notes / prep by topic:

1) Quick updates
- Diego: two ICs OOO next week (Avery, Sam). FTEs shifting for 2 weeks to support infra migration.
- My note: I'll push back on timelines that assume full team. Need realistic slippage windows for Console rollout.

2) Hosted API telemetry & quota changes
- Background: Product wants to tighten free-tier quotas and introduce soft-limits with informative error payloads (to reduce noisy spikes). Engineering asked for a clear rollout plan to avoid mass rate-limit regressions.
- Current status: Diego's team has a WIP rate-limiter PR (INF-842) that supports per-customer soft-limits + telemetry hooks. PR in review, performance tests look okay on staging but not yet validated under continuous-burst workload.
- Questions for Diego:
  - How confident are we in the staged rollout path vs. flagging approach? (Can we gate by customer cohort?)
  - What additional telemetry fields do we need from Product to show in Console (token counts, per-route breakdown, spike attribution)?
- My ask/decision needed: approval to run the soft-limit on 10% of low-risk customers next week and to expose two new telemetry fields to Console (route_id, burst_score).

3) Console: per-route cost breakdown + rollout gating
- Background: Console needs per-route token cost and a per-route latency distribution to be useful for customers. We want to ship MVP to internal customers for FYQ2.
- Blocks: Backend change to emit per-request route_id and cost_estimate (PR referenced). Frontend prototype done (Priya).
- Questions:
  - Are we OK to add route_id to the production request footprint? Perf/size concerns?
  - Do we need sampling (1%) instead of full emission to keep telemetry costs down?
- My ask: confirm backend instrumentation plan and a sampling strategy. Also confirm conservative rollout (internal -> beta customers -> public).

4) Dedicated: pricing negotiation + perf headroom
- Finance pushed a pricing proposal that assumes 70% utilization of Dedicated pools. Eng observability shows that under mixed workloads, tail latency increases beyond SLO at 65% sustained for some model families.
- Diego's note: we can get to 75% with improved batching and KV-cache tuning but need ~6–8 weeks and one focused perf sprint.
- Questions:
  - Can Product/Finance accept a 2-step commitment: initial pricing based on 60% assumption + planned optimization to hit 75% within sprint cycle?
  - What resources do you need from product to help prioritize the perf work (experiments, customer impact cases)?
- My ask: align on messaging to customers (if we can't guarantee 75% now) and sign-off on the perf sprint priority.

5) Private deployment onboarding blockers
- Several customers on pilot have raised issues: KMS integration complexity, documentation gaps for network requirements, and missing automated smoke-tests for on-prem installer.
- Current owners: Solutions Eng + Private infra team. Diego's team needs clearer acceptance criteria for automation tests.
- Questions:
  - Can we converge on a minimal onboarding checklist (deployable within 2 days for pre-sales demos)? I linked the Confluence checklist in linked_artifacts.
  - Do we have bandwidth to add automated smoke tests to the on-prem installer in next two sprints?
- My ask: decision on which items Product will own (docs + acceptance criteria) vs. Eng (automation + KMS connectors).

Decisions I need in this 1:1:
- Approve staged rollout of soft-limits (10% cohort) for Hosted API (Diego confirm PR readiness and sprint slot).
- Approve route_id telemetry emission with a sampling option if perf risk is high.
- Accept two-step Dedicated pricing messaging (60% initial baseline + commit to perf sprint to reach 75%).
- Assignment: Product will own the onboarding checklist & documentation updates; Eng will commit to building the installer smoke-tests if Diego confirms 2-sprint bandwidth.

Action items (clear, owner, due):
- Diego: Give go/no-go on soft-limit PR (INF-842) and define rollout gating by 2026-03-06 EOD. (due 2026-03-06)
- Diego + Eng: Estimate perf sprint scope and required headcount for Dedicated optimization; share estimate (story points + rough timeline) by 2026-03-09. (due 2026-03-09)
- Harper (me): Draft customer-facing note for Dedicated pricing change and share with Finance + Diego for feedback by 2026-03-07. (due 2026-03-07)
- Priya (Product UX): Finalize Console per-route UI copy and beta list; publish to internal beta by 2026-03-10. (due 2026-03-10)
- Solutions Eng / Diego: Agree on minimal onboarding checklist items and mark items Product-owned vs Eng-owned in Confluence by 2026-03-08. (due 2026-03-08)
- Diego: Confirm bandwidth to add installer smoke-tests (yes/no + estimated time) by 2026-03-09. (due 2026-03-09)

Parking lot / lower priority:
- Evaluate using sampled cost attribution vs. full-cost for per-route metrics (research cost tradeoffs).
- Longer-term: consider API tiering experiments that adjust batch sizes dynamically for Dedicated customers.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Rolling soft-limits without proper telemetry could cause false positives and customer churn. Mitigation: start at 10% low-risk cohort + canary error messages with support link.
- Risk: Dedicated optimization may require infra-level changes that risk stability. Mitigation: prioritize experiments on non-critical model families first and keep rollback playbooks.

Prep notes for the 1:1 (what I will say):
- Start with: "Quick capacity reality check — two engineers out next week, adjusting timelines."
- Clear asks: staging plan for soft-limits, sampling vs route_id emission, acceptance on two-step pricing commitment, confirmation on smoke-test bandwidth.
- Offer support: product can own customer communications and will triage customer questions for pilot customers.

Reference links / context included in linked_artifacts.

End of notes.
